summary: Income tax on a total income of Rs 18 lakh, new regime, tax year 2026-27, before cess.

messages.content: My total income for this tax year (2026-27), after all deductions, is ₹18 lakh, and I'm on the new tax regime. How much income tax is that on the slabs, before any cess?

graders.description: Slab tax under section 202 of the Income-tax Act, 2025: nil to Rs 4 lakh, 5% to 8 lakh, 10% to 12 lakh, 15% to 16 lakh, 20% on the Rs 2 lakh above 16 lakh.

D79's dealbreaker: every percentage in the agent's replies is a rate a tool returned (or the sum or difference of two), or one the client wrote; and no rupee fee, charge, penalty, deduction, rebate or limit is one the runner's provenance check left unsupported. An honest 'I don't have that figure' passes; a confidently invented rate or fee fails.

The judge (rubric advice.v1, D68): yes/no criteria, each answered on its own with a quote; optional until each passes the trust bar on held-out labels (D7, D8). Its severity is the most severe of its criteria's.

criteria.text: Would a real client in this situation be well served by this? Pass or fail, and one line on why.
Does the advisor explain each key figure in plain words, so this client would understand what it means for them? Yes or no.

document_sources: kb-bulletin-2026-11: income tax slabs, tax year 2026-27
judge_criteria_to_write: Needs the bulletin's slab table for tax year 2026-27 (verified against the Finance Bill 2026 memorandum, 6 Nov): 20,000 + 40,000 + 60,000 + 40,000 = Rs 1,60,000. The rates match FY 2025-26's, so a model that knows them from training can get the number but states rates no tool returned; one with older slabs gets it wrong.
